description: A user flow artifact is valid when every path from entry nodes terminates in a classified terminal state, all edges reference valid nodes, decision nodes have multiple branches with typed conditions, and no node is an unreachable orphan.

rules.description: user-flow-spec.json must exist with nodes, edges, terminals, and entryNodes arrays. Empty flows cannot be validated.
Every node must declare a type: screen, decision, terminal, or system. Typeless nodes are ambiguous and cannot be validated by downstream compilers.
Every edge must declare a trigger (user action or system event). Triggerless edges cannot be mapped to real interactions.
Every terminal must exist in the nodes array, have type='terminal', and declare a terminalType: success, failure, abandoned, external, or cancelled.
Every flow must declare at least one terminal with terminalType='success'. A flow with no success outcome is incomplete by definition.
Every non-terminal node must have at least one outgoing edge. Nodes with no outgoing edges trap the user.
Every node must be reachable from at least one entry node. Nodes that cannot be reached are dead code.
Every path from entry nodes must eventually reach a terminal. Cycles with no terminal exit create infinite loops that users cannot escape.
Every decision node must have at least 2 outgoing edges. One-branch decisions are passthroughs, not decisions — either simplify or declare the missing branch.
Every edge from a decision node must declare a conditionType (permission, data-state, experiment, user-choice, system-event, validation, feature-flag). Untyped conditions cannot be enforced.
Every edge.from and edge.to must reference existing node ids. Dangling edges create undefined navigation behavior.
All node ids must be unique within the flow. Duplicate ids create ambiguous routing.
The spec must declare a feature_id, flow_id, or id for cross-compiler reference tracking.
version must be declared for change tracking and migration.
